text:
Alex Laferriere scored the goal of the week in Montreal, a between-the-legs finish NHL.com floated as goal of the season. The rest of his season has been a lot of good chances and not much to show for it.

He has five goals on 10.1 expected goals (the quality of his chances), the biggest shortfall on this list, and he's shooting 6.9% against a normal of about 11%. His teammates have the same problem: the Kings have scored 5.4 fewer goals than expected with him out there. Both gaps tend to close.

The reason to take him seriously is his role. He's playing 19 minutes and 41 seconds a night, up from 18:19, and he's now on the ice for 74% of Los Angeles' power-play chances, up from 30% last season. His own chances are up sharply, 1.33 expected goals per 60 from 0.96, and the Kings get 57% of the five-on-five chances with him on. He also has 76 hits, which says he isn't just a shooter. A third-round pick out of Harvard, he's 25 and earning top-six minutes. Our range has him at 18 to 31 goals.
